name: page-2-community-garden
paragraphs: the Riverbend Community Garden committee have planned a neighborhood planting day for saturday, April 18, at 9:00 a.m. The event will take place beside the East Library on Maple Avenue , where there is many empty beds that need soil and seed. Last winter the irrigation pipe froze, and the maintence team were suppose to replace it but they didn't received the final valve until March. Because of that delay the the first group of volenteers must water seedlings by hand. Project lead Maria Chen said every helper should recieve a green wristband, a map, and one pair of gloves when they arrive. Each volunteers also need to sign the safety sheet before touching tools. The committee want the check-in line to move more quicker, so two tables will be setup near the blue storage shed one is for registered families and one is for walk-ins. no children under twelve may use shovels without an adult, however they can plant lettuce seeds in the raised beds.

The morning schedule will begins with a ten-minute orientation led by Omar Ruiz, then teams are moving to seperate work zones. Zone A will mix compost into six vegetable beds; Zone B clears weeds around the pollinator path; and Zone C are building two cedar benches. Organizers ordered 24 bags of compost, 18 tomato plants, 12 trays of lettuce, and four packets of sunflower seeds. They definately expect those supplies to last, although the inventory list don't include the herbs donated by Green Street Market. Anyone who brings a wheelbarrow should label it, because three identical red carts was lost at last years cleanup. The accessibility crew will accomodate guests who use wheelchairs by keeping the north gate open and laying rubber mats over the gravel. Between you and I, the south entrance is too steep and could of caused problems during the previous event. Lunch starts at 12:30 p.m.; sandwiches, fruit and water is provided but volunteers with allergies should bring there own meal.

after lunch, Maria and Omar will meeted each team near the tool station to review what was finished. The closing checklist asks leaders to count rakes, return unused seed, photograph the beds and report any injury even small ones. A local photographer from the Riverbend Gazette is attending, participants who do not want to appear in pictures should tell the check-in desk. The garden board hopes the day creates a safer growing space and helps neighbors learn practical skills, it also wants to collect ideas for a summer workshop series. A succesful event would leave all six beds planted, both cedar benches assembled, and the pollinator path free of litter. Before leaving every family should write one suggestion on the yellow feedback cards and put it inside the weatherproof box. the committee plans to publish results on Monday, April 20, but they hasn't chosen who will write the update. If rain becomes heavy the event moves to Saturday, April 25 at the same time, light rain will not cancel activities. Questions can be sent to garden coordinator Elena Park at the East Library information desk.
